identification.name: PHA (FDM 3D Printed)
identification.common_form_notes: 1.75 mm and 2.85 mm diameter filament, generally sold as a stiffer PLA-like alternative or as PLA/PHA blends (e.g. ColorFabb). Moisture-sensitive like PLA/nylon — dry at 60–70°C for 4–6 hours before printing. Also available as injection-moulding pellet grades (e.g. Telles Mirel™).
identification.notes: Polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA), a bacterially-fermented, fully biodegradable bioplastic family spanning Tm 40–180°C and 0–70% crystallinity depending on composition (Wikipedia). Mechanical and thermal property values below are from a MatWeb datasheet for Telles Mirel™ P1004, a general-purpose injection-moulding PHA resin — Telles (Metabolix/ADM joint venture) never sold PHA as printer filament and discontinued its Mirel line around 2016, so no filament-specific mechanical datasheet exists; P1004 is used as the best available proxy for bulk PHA resin behaviour, same approach as the PA12 entry blending a bulk-resin datasheet with process data. Chosen over the companion grade P1003 ("high modulus": 3.00 GPa tensile modulus, 4.0% elongation, 132°C HDT) because P1004 ("high toughness": 1.60 GPa tensile modulus, 7.0% elongation, 123°C HDT) is more ductile and its elongation falls inside salesplastics.com's generic FDM-PHA range (5–20%), a better match for the FDM use case this entry targets. Density (1.30 g/cm³, P1004) is a resin figure; commercial FDM filament is typically compounded to 1.23–1.25 g/cm³ per salesplastics.com, likely reflecting plasticizer/blend differences from a straight injection-moulding formulation — filament density will run slightly lower than stored here. Melting point stored as 160°C (the low end of both salesplastics.com's family-wide Tm range, 160–180°C, and MatWeb P1004's recommended processing melt-temperature window, 160–165°C — convergent evidence); the true value for any specific commercial filament varies with valerate content and blend ratio, so treat 160–180°C as the real uncertainty band rather than a precise value. Glass transition (0°C, low end of salesplastics.com's reported 0–5°C range) is similarly a family-wide range, not a P1004-specific measurement — MatWeb does not report Tg for P1004. usable_temp_range max (60°C) is salesplastics.com's as-printed FDM figure, not MatWeb's injection-moulded HDT data (63–123°C depending on load) — FDM parts have weaker inter-layer bonding than fully consolidated injection-moulded material and shouldn't be assumed to reach resin-level HDT; salesplastics.com does note specific PHB-rich formulations can reach ~120°C HDT after a secondary crystallization/annealing post-process, consistent with MatWeb's low-load (0.46 MPa) HDT of 123°C for unannealed P1004 — but this isn't the as-printed default. usable_temp_range min is not reported by either source and is left null rather than guessed. Poisson's ratio, thermal conductivity, specific heat, CTE, and Shore hardness are not reported by either source and are left null. Shear strength left null: von Mises derivation (UTS/√3) is reserved for ductile metals per project convention, not applied here. Ductility (7%, typical) is P1003/P1004's single-point MatWeb value; salesplastics.com's broader 5–20% range likely reflects variation across PHA/PHBV formulations rather than P1004 specifically. Electrical conductivity is nominally 0% IACS (International Annealed Copper Standard) — PHA, like other thermoplastics, is an electrical insulator, not a specific sourced measurement.

typical_usage: Compostable prototypes, packaging inserts, agricultural clips and plant pots, single-use fixtures, and educational/demonstration parts where biodegradability matters more than mechanical performance; food-contact items (verify specific filament brand's food-safety certification). Injection-moulded caps, closures, cutlery, and consumer packaging per the underlying Mirel resin's original target applications. Choose over PLA when compostability in home/industrial composting (not just industrial-only, as with PLA) or non-detectable biodegradation in soil/water is required; choose PETG or PLA instead when higher stiffness, wider material/colour availability, or lower cost is the priority.
